key_insight: PRISM shows that fixed, untrained neural features can support competitive anomaly detection without pretrained representations or neural weight optimization.
engineering_relevance: PRISM provides a prior-to-learning baseline for testing whether representation training adds value in tabular detection and visual anomaly localization.
method: Score anomalies using normal-reference Mahalanobis distances.
Use PRISM-T for tables and PRISM-V for dense visual localization.
evidence_signal: Across 47 ADBench datasets, PRISM-T achieved 86.4% mean AUROC (highest) and 65.9% mean AUPRC (second-highest); across 27 MVTec AD and VisA categories, PRISM-V achieved 90.4% image-level and 96.4% pixel-level mean AUROC.
watch_item: No neural training does not mean no fitting: Mahalanobis scoring still requires representative normal-reference statistics and numerically stable covariance estimation.
paper_title: How Far Can Untrained Neural Networks Go in Anomaly Detection? From Tables to Pixels
